summary.text: 过 means “to pass” or “to go across.” Its traditional graph 過 is analyzed as 辵, the walking element, plus 咼 as a sound element. The simplified form 过 has a long history as a variant of 過, though its precise graphic route is unresolved.

formation.text: The received Shuowen analysis describes traditional 過 as a phonosemantic compound: 辵 contributes the sense of movement, and 咼 supplies a sound cue. This is a historical dictionary analysis, not proof of the graph’s earliest composition. The simplified character 过 is a long-used variant of 過; a cursive route has been proposed, but the evidence here does not establish how that form developed.

components.text: 辶 is the left-side form of 辵 in regular script. In 過, 辵 contributes the idea of walking or movement; this is the received dictionary analysis.

咼 is identified as the phonetic element in 過. Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions place 咼 and 過 in the same proposed sound series, though their reconstructed sounds are similar rather than identical. Accounts of 咼’s internal shape and original referent are disputed.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese system, 咼 is reconstructed *kʰʷroːl and 過 *kloːl or *kloːls. Their similar but nonidentical forms support a proposed phonetic relationship; they are not an exact match.

history.text: The curated seal-script image illustrates the received Shuowen form and its 辵-plus-咼 analysis. It is a modern digital redraw, not an ancient artifact or evidence for the graph’s earliest composition.

The exact earliest form and composition remain unresolved here. A secondary account reports an oracle-bone form 𨒵 analyzed as 辵 plus 冎, but the proposed reading and development are not verified from primary inscription images; interpretations of 咼’s internal shape also differ.

过 is documented as a long-used common variant of 過 in later popular texts, and was listed as its simplified form in the 1964 table. The claim that it was adapted from 過’s cursive form is not independently confirmed here, so the precise graphic route remains uncertain.

uncertainties.text: The Shuowen component analysis is a received historical interpretation. The dossier does not establish the graph’s earliest composition, verify the reported oracle-bone analysis from primary images, or settle the original referent of 咼’s internal shape.

The sound comparison is a proposed historical relationship: the available Zhengzhang reconstructions differ in details, and values from other reconstruction systems in the dossier have not been independently verified here.
The precise graphic route from 過 to 过 is unresolved; evidence documents earlier variant use and later official standardization but does not establish a cursive pathway.

senses.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 過 as 度也, interpreted in the dossier as measuring or crossing a distance. The exact date of the earliest use is not established.
Classical citations document 過 used with the sense “exceed,” but their presence does not establish when this sense arose.
A later commentary treats “fault/error” as an extension of the passing sense. This is a historical interpretation; the timing and route of the development are not established by dated evidence here.
The common current meaning includes passing, passing through, and going across.

developments.text: A historical commentary explains “fault/error” as an extension of “passing”; the dossier does not establish when or precisely how the change occurred.

limitations.text: Dictionary examples record meanings such as visiting, excessive degree, and the experiential or completive particle, but do not establish when these senses first arose or a sequence connecting them. They are omitted from the main sense chronology.
The distinct level-tone and departing-tone readings are recorded in the dictionary tradition, but the evidence does not date their separation; this does not establish a separate semantic development.

overview.text: 过 means “to pass” or “go across.” Its traditional form combines a movement element with 咼 as a sound element. The simplified form has long been used as a variant, but its exact graphic route is unresolved.

components.text: The left-side form 辶 represents movement in this graph; its full form is 辵.
咼 is the proposed sound element; its reconstructed sound resembles, but does not exactly match, 過’s in the same system.

relationships.text: In traditional 過, 辶 is the positional form of 辵 and contributes the movement sense in the received analysis.
Traditional 過 is analyzed with 咼 as its phonetic element; the available same-system reconstructions are similar but not identical.
过 is documented as a long-used common variant of 過, with the precise graphic route unresolved.
The official simplified-character table maps 過 to 过; this standardization does not establish the form’s earlier graphic pathway.
